walks.name: Garden of Memories
walks.creator: chromic duo
walks.about:
Garden of Memories is an immersive AR soundwalk commissioned by Washington Performing Arts and Tregaron Conservancy, with support from the DC Commission on the Arts and Humanities. Bringing together site-specific stories, music, field recordings, and sound design, the work invites visitors to wander the Conservancy’s trails while discovering a hidden layer of stories and sounds connected to the landscape.

Inspired by the ways places become intertwined with the people and memories we carry, Garden of Memories explores how stories can transform a landscape into something deeply personal. A conversation shared on a familiar path, a loved one remembered through a daily walk, a place of comfort or solitude—these moments become part of the landscapes we inhabit. Alongside personal stories are tales drawn from folklore and music inspired by seasons, inviting visitors to reflection and encouraging them to slow down, listen closely, and make space for their own memories and questions. 

Take a walk through the Tregaron Conservancy, into a journey through the stories held within a landscape, and the memories it awakens within us.

walks.name: Listen to Chinatown
walks.creator: chromic duo
walks.about:
"Listen to Chinatown" is a site-specific Augmented Reality experience that takes listeners through Manhattan's Chinatown, following in the footsteps of the deep and expansive history of community members, and shares the intricate complexity of what it means to come "back home". 

Partnering with Chinatown’s BID, local businesses, spatial technology (AR) and cultural history experts Mott Street Girls, Listen to Chinatown brings stories beyond the storefront to life to celebrate Chinatown’s vibrant community and history. 

Listen to Chinatown was later adapted into a concert work, Homecoming, and premiered at Baryshnikov Arts Center.

walks.name: how fragile, we bloom
walks.creator: chromic duo
walks.about:
Citing poet Amanda Gorman’s “The Hill We Climb”, “how fragile, we bloom” takes listeners through a guided walk in the Herbert & Hyonja Abrons Woodland trail at Wave Hill Public Gardens, created in collaboration with their Art, Community, Education and Science (ACES) youth interns.

Alongside Chromic Duo's sound design, narration and composition, stories from the youths have been incorporated into a site-specific, meditative soundwalk that invites audiences to reflect upon this current moment in history. The youths' stories speak to individual and collective experiences, creating a storytelling capsule. Through communal creation and connection, Chromic Duo provides a platform for Wave Hill visitors to contemplate the ways that seasons bring change, their own relationships to nature and the larger community, and ultimately, how to support one another through times of uncertainty, and build a future arched towards collective liberation.
